> 歸妹。征凶，無攸利。

Hexagram 54 is about marrying off a younger daughter, and both of its difficult characters are commonly misread.

## 歸 means going to the husband's house

說文: 歸，女嫁也 — a woman marrying.

And the direction has to be kept: in the 易, 歸 is "to go to the husband's household," not "to return."

Being married off is called 歸 because the woman's 家 is at the husband's house.

So the hexagram is not about coming home. It is about arriving at a house that was not yours.

## 娣 is a position

娣 is the secondary wife who accompanies the bride — second in rank.

In pre-Qin aristocratic marriage, a niece or younger sister came along as 媵. This was the institution, not an indignity.

So 初九's 歸妹以娣 is not a put-down. It is a place: someone standing in the second seat.

And that is the whole subject of the hexagram: what can and cannot be done from the second seat.

## 跛, 眇

跛: one foot impaired, walking uneven. 眇: one eye impaired, seeing incompletely.

Neither is an insult here. Both are images: a person in an off-centre position can still walk and still see — just not all of it.

跛能履，征吉 and 眇能視，利幽人之貞: the damaged one can still do the thing, and that is enough.

## 須: waiting

須 has three readings: to wait; a term for a low-ranking concubine (通 媭); or elder sister.

This book takes "to wait." 歸妹以須 — the marriage delayed a long time.

And it reads better than the usual gloss ("wanting a principal wife's rites, greedy"), because it is about time, not ambition: having waited too long, she goes back and enters as 娣 — 反歸以娣.

Which is the saddest line in the chapter and requires no moralizing: the wait itself changed the rank.

## 月幾望

幾: near. 望: the full moon (the fifteenth).

月幾望 — the moon almost full.

The same phrase appears once more in the book, in 小畜上九, and there the verdict is 君子征凶.

Same degree of fullness, one bad and one good, and the difference is who is getting full.

## 帝乙歸妹，其君之袂不如其娣之袂良

六五: the emperor marries off his daughter, and the principal bride's sleeve is not as fine as her attendant's.

袂: the sleeve, standing for the dress.

The higher-ranked one dresses more plainly than the lower. And the verdict is 月幾望，吉 — nearly full, and good.

Which is the hexagram's turn: rank is not displayed. The one with the higher place wears the lesser sleeve, and that is why the moon does not overflow.

## 女承筐無實，士刲羊無血

Top line: the woman holds the basket and there is nothing in it; the man kills the sheep and there is no blood.

Two ritual acts, both empty. The vessels are there, the motions are there, and nothing is in them.

Which is the closing image of 歸妹 and its exact form of failure: not the wrong rank, not the wrong timing — the rite performed with no content.

## 永終知敝

The 象: 君子以永終知敝 — last to the end, and know the wearing-out.

永終: to endure to the end. 敝: a garment worn to ruin, extended to decay.

知敝 is not "know the drawbacks." It is knowing that this thing will get old, will fray, will not be as it is now.

Know that first, and it can be kept.

## The test

Take a relation or a role you entered from the second seat. Ask two questions the hexagram asks: was it the rank you took, or the rank you were given? And is the basket actually holding something, or is the motion being performed?
